title: The Pool I Feared
intro: 十歲那年的溺水經歷，讓他十年不敢下水。高三這年，他決定面對那座泳池。
passage:
When I was ten, I nearly drowned at a hotel pool. The memory never [[1]]: the cold water closing over my head, the silent panic, and a lifeguard pulling me out just in time. After that, I refused to go near any pool, lake or sea. My friends [[2]] me, but I always found an excuse — exams, tiredness, the weather.
Last September, however, I entered my final year of high school and suddenly felt [[3]] of my fear. It was not the fear itself that troubled me, but the way it had quietly [[4]] into other corners of my life. I avoided speaking in public. I gave up before trying difficult questions. Somewhere along the way, 'I can't swim' had become 'I can't [[5]] risks'.
So I made a deal with myself: ten swimming lessons, no excuses. On the first morning I stood at the edge of the pool, heart [[6]], fingers cold. My coach, a patient woman in her fifties, simply said, 'Sit on the step. Just breathe.' For twenty minutes I did nothing but breathe and watch the water move. It felt [[7]] — like a punishment — but I followed her instructions.
Week by week, she added one small task: put my face in the water; blow bubbles; float with her hand [[8]] my back. Each skill looked ridiculously small on paper, yet each one asked me to [[9]] the water a little more. One afternoon in November, without being asked, I pushed off the wall and glided — arms forward, face down, bubbles rising. When I [[10]], I had crossed half the pool.
I did not cry, though I wanted to. What moved me was not the distance I covered but the [[11]] that fear shrinks when you face it in small, repeated steps. The pool had not changed; I had.
My exam results that year did improve, but that is not the [[12]] of this story. The real lesson came on a December evening, when I stood at the edge of the deep end, looked down at the blue water, and felt — for the first time in eight years — not [[13]] but calm. I still respect the water. I no longer let it [[14]] my choices.
Courage, I now believe, is not the absence of fear. It is the decision that something else — growth, freedom, curiosity — [[15]] more than your fear does.

questions.note: 下文詳述記憶的細節（冰冷的水、無聲的恐慌），說明記憶從未「褪去」；faded 最貼切；returned、deepened、changed 與「記憶清晰如昨」的展開不符。
「但我總找藉口拒絕」說明朋友常「取笑/打趣」我不敢下水；teased 合乎語境；praised、envied、supported 均為正面詞，與找藉口迴避的行為矛盾。
升入高三「突然對自己的恐懼感到羞恥」，才下定決心改變；feel ashamed of the fear 合乎成長敘事；proud、confident 為正面詞，矛盾；aware 不與 of my fear 構成行動動機。
下文列舉逃避演講、放棄難題，說明恐懼已「蔓延」到生活其他角落；spread into 最貼切；disappeared、dropped 與列舉的負面影響矛盾。
take risks 為固定搭配「冒險」；make/get/bring 均不與 risks 搭配。
heart pounding 意為「心怦怦直跳」，描寫站在池邊的緊張；aching（疼痛）、breaking、burning 與恐懼場景不符。
「只是坐著呼吸二十分鐘」當時感覺像懲罰，覺得毫無意義（pointless），但還是照做——與 but I followed her instructions 的轉折呼應；helpful、relaxing 與 like a punishment 矛盾。
教練的手托在背部「下方」幫助漂浮，beneath my back 準確；above 在上方（會壓沉）、beyond、across 均不符合托扶的動作。
每個小任務都要求我多「信任」水一分，呼應結尾 no longer let it control me；fear 與任務遞進的正面意義相反。
滑行後起身，發現自己已游過半個泳池；stood up 合乎動作順序；gave up、woke up 與語境不符。
真正的收穫是「發現」恐懼會在逐步面對中縮小；discovery 與 What moved me was... 的領悟呼應；excuse、promise、memory 無法概括這一道理。
「成績進步不是這個故事的重點」，the point of this story 為慣用表達；ending、secret、cost 與 not...but the real lesson 的對照不符。
not afraid but calm「不再恐懼，而是平靜」，直接呼應全文的恐懼主題；proud、tired、bored 與八年怕水的敘事線不對應。
「我尊重水，但不再讓它控制我的選擇」，control 呼應開頭恐懼蔓延到生活各處的主題；share、record、explain 均脫離語境。
matters more than...「比恐懼更重要」，呼應 courage 的定義句；costs（花費）、weighs（更重）、arrives 均與 the decision that something else... 的語義不符。
